report.summary: Reviewed only the supplied source packet: lib/assessment-obligations.ts and tests/assessment-obligations.test.ts. The cycle-20 English sentence split (a '.' followed by whitespace and an uppercase letter, with abbreviation/decimal/path/URL/email safeguards), quote masking for operation detection (withoutQuotedData), exact UTF-16 clause refs, the over-limit fallback, and strict re-derivation look coherent within their stated bounded scope. The parent verdict, acceptance and payment are never derived from these records: states are limited to execution_not_verified, source_review_required and needs_clarification. I found no reachable P1/P2 defect within the bounded-detector framing. The previous class-instance finding is rejected: plainData rejects class-prototype (non-Object/null/Array) values, and no alternative path constructs or accepts such values. I found no P1/P2 findings. One P3 note is retained on the detection scope: masking drops every quoted span from kindsFor, so an operation that is genuinely the requirement itself, if stated inside quotes, lands as unclassified/needs_clarification (visible and non-authoritative) rather than as an execution_not_verified obligation. This is a documented trade-off (test at line 64), not a verdict or payment error.

findings.title: Operations stated only inside quotation marks become unclassified clarification instead of a typed non-executing obligation
findings.evidence: kindsFor calls withoutQuotedData (line 83) and runs all detectors on the masked text. A requirement like 'The contact form must "send email to the owner".' therefore detects nothing and falls to line 92. absent any source_text scope hit, it becomes 'unclassified' (needs_clarification) rather than 'email_delivery' (execution_not_verified). The record stays visible with full wording, and the presentation copy for 'unclassified' (line 158) asks for clarification without inferring a promise. The state is conservative and cannot assert execution or success. This is the intended masking trade-off (test lines 64-69), but the user-visible type is weaker than for the same wording without quotes.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: source = 'The contact form must "send email to the owner".'. clausesFor yields one clause. withoutQuotedData blanks "send email to the owner", so EMAIL, SUBMISSION and WRITE do not match. kinds is empty, and assessmentEvidenceScope finds no source_text context, so the single item is unclassified/needs_clarification. Its next step asks for agreed check and evidence, not email operations. No verdict is derived.
findings.suggestion: No required change for safety. If the product wants operation typing for quoted requirement text, add a bounded fallback that runs detectors on the unmasked clause only when the masked clause yields only 'unclassified', keeping state needs_clarification or execution_not_verified. This needs a schema/version decision, not an in-place retrofit.

limitations: Read-only static review of the two supplied files only. No tests, typecheck, build, or runtime execution was performed or claimed.

Only the detector/validator and their tests were in scope. The UI component (app/components/AssessmentObligations.tsx), assessmentEvidenceScope, exactCopyLiteral, sourceLiteralDirective, staticMarkupDirective, and the parent verdict/acceptance/payment code paths were not supplied, so I could not verify cross-module reachability.

Acceptance is by design a bounded finite detector, not a fully general English/Chinese parser nor a real-human evaluation. Behavior depends on the stated English-only sentence rule ('.' + whitespace + uppercase) and finite abbreviation/dotted-token lists. Unknown abbreviations or identifiers that end in '.' before an uppercase word may still over-split. That was not shown to cause a wrong verdict, and the result keeps exact clauses.
No award-comparison or superiority assessment was requested or made; this review addresses correctness reachability only.
Files are not published or frozen by this review; shared v1 status is unchanged.
